messages:
leah: Heads-up: premerge CI for infra change PR #11012 (terraform module updates) included SAST warnings and a DAST proof that looks like a transient RBAC escalation exposed a decrypted config snippet. artifact: gs://ci/11012/scan.json

omar: can you paste the snippets and the terraform diff?

leah: snippet and plan excerpt below:
```
SAST: infra/terraform/modules/keystore/main.tf:45 - iam_binding allows serviceAccount:deployer-ci -> grants roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter (rule RDX-TF-KMS-01)
DAST: POST /internal/health -> response body contains 'redis_pass: <evaluated>' proof
TF PLAN (partial):
+ google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding.binding["deployer-ci"]
    role: "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
    members: ["serviceAccount:deployer-ci@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
artifact: gs://ci/11012/scan.json
```

toni: tagging @vivian (infra)  did we intend to grant decrypt role to deployer-ci in this roll?

vivian: no. The module was updated to centralize bindings but we relied on a variable that defaulted to true for including decrypt grants for convenience in staging. That default should've been false. Also, our audit sink for keystore actions has a 1h delay due to a recent logging pipeline change  may explain why we can't see immediate audit evidence.

security-bot: Scan summary for build 11012: 1 HIGH (improper KMS role in terraform), 3 MED (unsafe keystore patterns), 2 LOW. Suggested triage: block the merge, reproduce in a sandbox, pull terraform plan + keystore audit slice, and create an incident ticket if audit gaps exist.

infra-oncall: I'm on-call; will repro in sandbox and try to replay the plan with a dry-run to see what grants would be applied. Also will check the logging pipeline to surface the audit entries.

omar: this is a mix of SDLC and infra config: SAST flagged the TF policy, but DAST shows runtime exposure. We should assume the grant applied at some point in staging and caused the exposure. Repro plan: 1) dry-run apply in a sandbox 2) repro DAST against sandbox with and without grant 3) pull any audit logs available 4) revert change in PR if confirmed.

leah: I've blocked the PR and added the terraform plan output to RED-11500. Created ticket RED-11500 and linked the CI artifact + proposed rollback. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RED-11500

vivian: found the logging pipeline change: a sink filter in logging-prod queued keystore audit entries for batching and introduced delay. I'm pulling raw audit logs from the keystore admin console and will attach to RED-11500. We should treat this as an audit-gap incident if logs don't show expected grant activity.

omar: also note the terraform module default is the root cause: a boolean var decrypt_grants = true used in staging-only configs. We need to change default to false and require explicit opt-in. Propose adding a terraform-linter rule (TFSEC pattern) that flags any module that creates roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter without an explicit justification tag.

toni: for immediate mitigation, can infra revert the binding or remove the member in staging? We should remove decrypt capability if it's not required.

infra-oncall: I can remove the binding in staging now. Doing dry-run: `terraform apply -target=google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding.binding -refresh-only` then plan destroy for that binding. Posting timestamped action in ticket.

vivian: audit export attached to RED-11500: no decrypt grant entry in the window because of the logging delay, but we found a weld point: the deployer-ci principal requested a decrypt on 2025-04-18T09:12Z which returned 200 for one request. That suggests grant existed transiently or the CI pipeline used another service account with broader privileges. I'm investigating service account overlap.

leah: important: we need to correlate the CI job identities. Omar, can you grep CI logs for service account email used during the 09:12Z job? Maybe deployer-ci impersonation happened.

omar: running that now. quick grep shows that a pipeline step used `impersonate: ci-operator@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in the rollout job. That account had a broader role added by an older automation patch. Looks like two different accounts were in play. I'll attach logs.

security-bot: Triage checklist reminder: ensure ticket references are present in keystore-change, rotate any keys if exposure is confirmed, update SDLC policy to block terraform plans that add decrypt roles without two-approver sign-off.

toni: action items on RED-11500: vivian -> attach audit slice + fix logging pipeline, infra-oncall -> remove binding in staging, omar -> correlate CI principal and attach logs, leah -> coordinate PR rollback and policy follow-ups. ETA initial rollback in 1h.

vivian: fixed logging pipeline filter, re-ingesting backlog. attached raw keystore admin logs and the audit slice to RED-11500. Also found an automation script `ci/iam/assign_roles.sh` that incorrectly promoted ci-operator to kms.decrypter in a previous rollout. Opening PR to patch and add tests.

omar: confirmed the decrypt request at 09:12Z was from ci-operator, not deployer-ci. ci-operator had role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter via automation PR #9934. I've attached the CI log snippet to RED-11500.

infra-oncall: binding removed from staging at 09:48Z and I confirmed DAST repro no longer shows evaluated config. Also kicked a premerge re-run for the PR after removing the binding.

leah: good. we should still rotate the affected key to be safe given a decrypted request occurred. vivian, can you coordinate a key rotation and include a minimal rotation playbook (who approves, who runs, how to backfill audit)?

vivian: will rotate the key in staging and create RED-11501 for key rotation activity and notes. Attaching rotation plan and expected downtime (none for current usage) and will notify impacted teams.

om ar: (typo) omar: also recommend adding a premerge TFSEC check that fails on new google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding resources granting decrypt without a change_note or ticket reference. I'll draft the check and PR it to devex.

security-bot: Automated recommendation: add PLCY-TF-01 (block decrypt grants in terraform without ticket and two approvers), PLCY-AUD-02 (alert on missing keystore audit entries during deployment window), and a CI check to correlate terraform plans with keystore-change entries.

toni: also add a developer checklist item: never assume default booleans for security-sensitive grants; require explicit opt-in and human review. We'll add this to the SDLC security checklist.

leah: summarizing: PR blocked, binding removed, key rotation planned (RED-11501), automation patch in progress to avoid accidental ci-operator grants, logging pipeline fixed, and policy proposals drafted. I'll write a short postmortem stub in RED-11500 and schedule a 30min retro with infra + security tomorrow.

infra-oncall: confirmed premerge re-run shows no high sev findings now. Marking the staging verification step complete in RED-11500.

vivian: patch for `ci/iam/assign_roles.sh` opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1108 (adds tighten checks and test harness).

om ar: (typo) omar: drafted TFSEC rule PR: https://github.com/redwood/devex/pull/401 - PLCY-TF-01. Needs review.

security-bot: Thread archived to RED-11500. Don't forget to add the incident tag and link RED-11501 for key rotation artifacts.

leah: thanks everyone. Closing slack thread; we'll keep RED-11500 open until the retro and policy changes land. :white_check_mark:
